sentences.text: The petitioner is the 1st accused in S.T.No.596 of 2009 pending on the files of the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (Economic Offences) Court, Ernakulam.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (Economic Offences) Court, Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In the aforesaid case, he is being proceeded against for having committed offences punishable under Sections 2(ia), 7(i)(v) and read with Section 16 (1) (a) (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as "the PFA Act" for short) and read with Rule 29 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as "the PFA Rules" for short).
2. The prosecution allegation is that on 16.03.2009 at about 12.00 noon, the Food Inspector visited the supermarket, where the petitioner was working as the Manager of the enterprises, and collected samples of Banana Wafers, which were kept in the shop for sale to the public.
The seized items were sampled and labelled in accordance with law and one part of the sample was forwarded to the Public Analyst.

The Public Analyst, in his report dated 18.04.2009, came to the conclusion that the sample contains added synthetic Food Colour Tartrazine (Colour Index 19140) which is in contravention of Rule 29 of the PFA Rules and is, therefore, adulterated.
The said analysis report is produced as Annexure-2.
Thereafter, based on the said report, Annexure-1 complaint was preferred before the learned Magistrate.
3. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.
4. The contention of the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner revolves on the interpretation of Sections 23(1A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act.

It is submitted that relying on the ratio of the judgment of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector and another [2010 (4) KLT 706 (SC)], a Division Bench of this Court in Rasheed N.K. V Food Inspector, Thalasserry (2016 (1) KLD 704) has laid down that Sections 23(1A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act are mandatory and any prosecution instituted under the Act, in violation of the said provisions, will have to necessarily bite the dust.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector and another [2010 (4) KLT 706 (SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Rasheed N.K. V Food Inspector, Thalasserry (2016 (1) KLD 704)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is forcefully urged that method of analysis is not a validated one as prescribed under Section 23(1A)(hh) and the laboratory, where the analysis was conducted, was not a defined one for such examination under Section 23(1A)(ee) of the Act.
5.
In the case on hand, Annexure-1 complaint was laid solely on the strength of the Annexure-2 Form III report of the Public Analyst.
The said report is dated 18.04.2009.
It was found that the food item did not conform to the standard prescribed as per Item No.A-16.28 of Appendix B of the Rules, 1955.

The Division Bench in Rasheed N.K. (supra), after interpreting the various provisions of the PFA Act, 1957, in line with the pronouncement of the Apex Court in Pepsico Case (supra), has held that in order for the Analyst report to become the basis for launching a prosecution, the analysis of the food has to be conducted in a laboratory defined under S.23(1A)(ee) of the Act.

6. It is beyond cavil that the PFA Act, 1954 was repealed as per the notification issued by the Central Government dated 04/08/2011 by virtue of powers under S.97(1) of the FSS Act and the same had come into force with effect from 05/08/2011.

It has been held in Rasheed N.K. (supra) that till the K. Reghu vs Food Inspector on 4 June, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125119879/
2 repealing of PFA Act, 1954, no laboratory had been defined in terms of the provision under S.23(1A)(ee).

entities.text: K. Reghu vs Food Inspector on 4 June, 2019 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand, the report is dated 18.04.2009, which in other words, means that the laboratory, where the analysis was conducted, could not have been a defined lab.
If that be the case, the taking of cognizance on the basis of the said report cannot be sustained.
7. Hence the continuance of the prosecution on the basis of Annexure-1 complaint cannot be nothing, but an abuse of process of law.

In the result this petition is allowed and all further proceedings in S.T.No.595 of 2009 pending on the files of the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (Economic Offences) Court, Ernakulam, will stand quashed.
